Igor Stravinsky. A Russian-born composer, pianist and conductor widely considered one of the most influential and versatile musical figures of the twentieth century.

Stravinsky's career was marked by dramatic stylistic shifts. He began with his early Russian nationalist period, moved through a cool, structured Neoclassical phase, and ended in a rigorous serialist style. He achieved international fame through his collaborations with Sergei Diaghilev's Ballets Russes in Paris.

His Russian period produced three landmark ballets. The Firebird came in 1910, followed by Petrushka in 1911, and then The Rite of Spring in 1913. These works utilized polytonality, complex meters, and driving, primitive rhythms. The premiere of The Rite of Spring became legendary for triggering a full-scale riot in the audience due to its aggressive rhythms and avant-garde choreography.

The Rite of Spring depicts a pagan sacrifice in prehistoric Russia. It's famous for its opening bassoon solo in its highest register and its polyrhythmic "Augurs of Spring" chord. Petrushka tells the story of a tragic puppet brought to life, characterized by the Petrushka chord, a combination of C-major and F-sharp-major triads representing the puppet's dual human-puppet nature.

Around 1920, Stravinsky entered his Neoclassical period, a reaction against Romantic excess that sought inspiration from eighteenth-century Classical structures. During this time he composed the ballet Pulcinella, based on themes attributed to Pergolesi, as well as the opera-oratorio Oedipus Rex and the choral-orchestral Symphony of Psalms. The Soldier's Tale, a theatrical work for narrator and a small chamber ensemble of seven instruments, depicts a soldier who trades his violin to the devil for wealth. His major English opera, The Rake's Progress, premiered in 1951 with a libretto by W.H. Auden and Chester Kallman, inspired by William Hogarth's series of paintings.

Around 1950, Stravinsky adopted the twelve-tone method developed by his rival Arnold Schoenberg, entering his Serialist period. This lasted until his death in 1971, resulting in late works like the Requiem Canticles and Agon.

Stravinsky was a cosmopolitan figure whose life spanned major historical shifts. He fled Russia during World War One, lived in France, and eventually emigrated to the United States during World War Two, settling in Los Angeles. His innovative use of rhythm, particularly metric modulation and sudden accents, influenced nearly every subsequent twentieth-century composer. He was a close friend of intellectual figures such as writer Aldous Huxley and artist Pablo Picasso, who designed costumes for Pulcinella. Stravinsky studied orchestration under Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov, linking him to the Russian Romantic tradition.
